h: Why One Visit Rarely Feels Like Enough
p: There's a pattern with obstacle-course parks. First visits are all about surviving. Second visits are when people start working out technique, like how to swing your body to reach the next hold or where to place your feet on a wobbly section. By the third or fourth, kids are often clearing bits that defeated them at the start, and that sense of progress is hugely satisfying.

If your children love it, look into whether there are regular classes or memberships, as some parks run these for kids who want to train properly. It's a good way to build strength, balance and confidence.

Leeds is packed with things to round off the day. The Royal Armouries on the waterfront is free to visit and full of armour, weapons and stories from across the centuries. Roundhay Park is a vast green space with lakes, woodland and Tropical World, where you can wander among butterflies, reptiles and meerkats. Temple Newsam has a grand house, parkland and Home Farm, a working rare-breeds farm that little ones adore, while Kirkstall Abbey offers peaceful ruins by the River Aire.
Whatever you choose, it's a good idea to schedule something calmer after your session. Your arms will thank you.
